summary: Tested the new auth (email code + session cookie, Clerk removed) and invoices for every payment kind, on both backend and frontend, plus regression checks on card thumbnails and the template designer. Backend: 39 of 40 pytest tests pass. The 1 failure is a real security issue: the IP rate limit trusts the client-sent X-Forwarded-For header. Covered: /auth/config (google=false), /auth/google/start returns 503, invalid email returns 422, the per-email limit returns 429 without sending a code, verify with no code or an expired code returns 400, a wrong code returns 400 with 'N tries left' (4..1), the 5th wrong code invalidates the code (the correct code then gets 429), and a correct code sets an fc_session cookie (HttpOnly, Secure). Email is normalised to lowercase. Each code works only once. /auth/session works, logout deletes the session in the DB and clears the cookie, then /api/me returns 401. Existing user qa.admin is matched by email (user_ id, super_admin). A new user gets a u_ id. Admin revoke-sessions and suspend both remove sessions, and a suspended user who signs in again gets 403 on /api/me. Invoices: /me/payments/{id}/invoice returns 200 for the owner and 404 for another user, the admin invoice endpoint works, and the PDF builds. I ran notify_paid in-process with the email send captured (nothing sent) for plan, pack, watermark and storybook: all 4 got a 'receipt' email with the invoice number in the details and a PDF attachment. One real OTP was sent to test_otp_send_iter2@example.com (email_log shows sent via smtp). Frontend: signed-out visits to /dashboard and /create redirect to sign-in/sign-up. The Google button is hidden. On /sign-in (otp/request mocked in the browser to avoid sending email): the code step, change email, resend, and wrong-code toast ('4 tries left') work. The correct code redirects to /dashboard, the user menu shows the email, the cookie is httpOnly, and sign out goes to /sign-in with the session cleared. /admin works with the admin cookie. The template list and the design editor (boxes, inspector) render. The Invoice button in the dashboard billing history downloads TEST-2026-UI001.pdf.

critical.issue: The IP rate limit uses the first value of X-Forwarded-For, which the client controls. The ingress appends the real IP instead of replacing the header. I sent X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.x and the server stored the key otp-ip:203.0.113.x. An attacker can change this header on every request to get past the 10-per-IP limit on code requests and the 30-per-IP limit on verify, for example to spam codes to many addresses through the live SMTP. Fix: use the last value in X-Forwarded-For (the one the ingress adds), or the right-most untrusted hop, or request.client.host.

minor.issue: CORS_ORIGINS='*' is combined with allow_credentials=True. Starlette then echoes back any Origin with credentials allowed. The cookie is SameSite=Lax at the app level, but the preview ingress rewrites it to SameSite=None; Partitioned, so any site could make credentialed API calls in preview. Set explicit origins.
tries is read and then incremented in separate steps (not atomic). Parallel wrong guesses can go past MAX_TRIES. Use find_one_and_update with $inc and check the value it returns.
The pattern is checked before trimming, so an email with leading or trailing spaces is rejected with 422. The frontend trims, so this only affects API clients.

Leftover Clerk code: except requests.RequestException can never trigger now, and the 'Could not reach the auth provider' message no longer applies. /api/clerk/ is still in GATE_OPEN, and revoke_clerk_sessions and the clerk settings view are still there.
If the provider is switched to 'emergent', attachments are silently dropped, so receipts would arrive without the invoice PDF.

rca of the issue: XFF spoofing: _ip() takes headers['x-forwarded-for'].split(',')[0]. The K8s/Cloudflare ingress adds the real client IP to the existing header instead of replacing it, so the first value is whatever the client sent. Reproduce: POST /api/auth/otp/request with header X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.9, then check db.auth_rate for key 'otp-ip:203.0.113.9'. Fix: use the right-most hop, or a configured number of trusted proxies.
